note: Adapted from the original description of Termes simplicidens by Sjöstedt (1900), originally in German; the alate is recorded as unknown in the original; antennal segment counts, mandible lengths and the upper limit of total length could not be recovered because of OCR damage and are therefore not recorded; biological notes and specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish brown or yellowish red, frons paler and tinged with yellow, rounded-rectangular, narrowed and lowered anteriorly; occipital region arched, with rounded corners; occiput and sides broadly and roundly passing into the underside; dorsal surface of head flatly convex; submentum wider than the lateral parts, slightly narrowed anteriorly; frons slightly flattened, with a few small pits, truncate anteriorly; fontanelle absent; mandibles slightly curved upwards, slender, about half head length, weakly sickle-shaped, apex incurved and pointed; inner margin of left mandible with a sharp ridge from below to about the middle, a free sharp point projecting above the ridge; right mandible toothless; labrum lingulate, with a few hairs at apex, concolorous with head; antennae yellowish red, with pale green annulations, basal segment largest, basal segment and second segment bare, outer segments gradually slightly longer and again slightly shorter towards apex; head with a few hairs; pronotum hexagonally oval, anterior lobe distinctly notched at middle, lateral parts concave and slightly depressed, sides and posterior margin rather straight, posterior margin slightly incurved at middle; mesonotum transversely oval, anterior and posterior margins flattened, sides slightly upturned and rounded, narrower than pronotum; metanotum of about the same shape but shorter and wider; whole body rather densely covered with brown hairs, yellowish brownish white together with the legs; abdomen oval, dorsally convex, laterally compressed; last tarsal segment very long, about three times the sum of the remaining segments. A smaller soldier caste may also exist. Total length more than 10 mm, head including mandibles 4 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The worker is immediately distinguished from those of all other species by its peculiar fontanelle structure: the middle of the head bears a very distinct depression whose floor ends in an oval ring, the part within the ring being slightly raised and bearing a ridge running along the longitudinal axis of the head; head reddish brown, the frons above the clypeus and the clypeus alike pale yellow; from the frons over the vertex backwards there are often two pale stripes, sometimes only weakly marked, and one similar stripe on each side of the head; clypeus rather large, oval, flattened anteriorly, its anteroposterior length slightly greater than the antennal basal segment, with a dark line at the middle and bounded on each side by a dark brown spot; hairs of head and clypeus very sparse, whereas the large labrum is densely hairy; the first two teeth of the mandibles equal in size; antennae 19-segmented, third segment smallest, basal segment about as long as the three following segments together, each segment brown with a pale ring; anterior lobe of pronotum large, upturned, very distinctly notched at the middle; anterior corner of the posterior lobe deflexed, contracted, broadly rounded and concave, sides almost straight and sloping backwards, posterior margin rather wide, distinctly incurved at the middle; mesonotum oval, lateral parts wide, middle slightly convex, posterior margin slightly concave; metanotum wider and shorter, anterior margin rounded, posterior margin flattened, sides deflexed and concave anteriorly; hind tibia slightly longer than femur; last tarsal segment twice the sum of the remaining segments; whole body together with the legs yellowish, covered with rather strong reddish brown hairs. Probably the major worker of this species. Body length 6–8 mm, head width 2.2 mm.
